strings.MEX_CountryInfo_Content_desc.1:
The presidency of Lázaro Cárdenas was a new beginning for the languishing Mexican Revolution. The collectivization of farmland into “ejidos” had brought significant change to the countryside, landmark efforts to educate the country had begun, and the popular movement itself was incorporated into a united, corporatist organization - Partido de la Revolución Mexicana. Under his firm hand, Mexico was at last moving towards socialism.

The biggest event of Cárdenas' sexenio was the 1938 nationalization of oil. At a stroke, Mexico reclaimed its sovereign rights to its greatest resources. However, this caused tremendous outrage, mostly with the oil companies in the United States.
strings.MEX_CountryInfo_Content_desc.2:
Faced with the tensions from the oil expropriation, the next president, Manuel Ávila Camacho, would adopt a more moderate approach. He ended the thorny issues with the Church and rolled back many of the outright socialist policies like socialist education. This did not seem to placate the new American government, however, which led to a personal rift that kept Mexico from fully committing to the western allies. Mexico would never join the war, and often resisted pressure from the United States to fully eliminate falangist and fascist groups.

The war did, however, affect Mexico. The higher commodity prices and lack of European exports convinced the PRM the way to a brighter future lay in industrialization and opening up to the global markets. And the tensions with the United States convinced them a new ally was needed in the hemisphere.
strings.MEX_CountryInfo_Content_desc.3:
President Miguel Alemán was responsible for the massive postwar shift in the Revolution. A new opening to the Japanese brought in a new partner that would reduce reliance on the Americans. Foreign investors in industry and tourism would also grow the economy, leading to the Mexican Miracle and rampant corruption.

At home, Alemán would solidify his power through the new Dirección Federal de Seguridad, a secret police force. But perhaps his greatest accomplishment was the reformation of the PRM into the Partido Revolucionario Institucional, and the solidification of Mexico into a de facto one party state.
strings.MEX_CountryInfo_Content_desc.4:
After a controversial election in 1952, Adolfo Ruiz Cortines would seek to restore faith in the Revolution by tamping down on the excesses of Alemán. Through fighting corruption and building infrastructure, Ruiz Cortines kept the Miracle going. However, it was clear more was needed.

Providing a velvet glove and an iron fist, Adolfo López Mateos had overseen populist policies and violent crackdowns since 1958. He brought Mexico onto the world stage by promoting it as a center of neutrality and reason. However, his vision still faced massive tests.
strings.MEX_CountryInfo_Content_desc.5:
If there is an “ideology” to the PRI it is based around maintaining order through left populist handouts, state capitalist economics, and brutal repression. This is represented first and foremost by the second most powerful man in Mexico, Gustavo Díaz Ordaz, the Interior Secretary. Holding this role often means he manages the state apparatus to buy loyalty and snuff out dissent.

An heir apparent like Ordaz needs the party structure to help him win elections with some degree of legitimacy. The man responsible for that is Alfonso Corona del Rosal, former General and head of the PRI. Longtime party functionaries like him are key to ensuring the Revolution retains its course.
strings.MEX_CountryInfo_Content_desc.6:
The economic growth that has solidified the PRI's hold on power can be traced to one man: Finance Secretary Antonio Ortiz Mena. He has been given a free hand to run the economy through export focused state capitalism by successive governments, and it has worked extremely well, guaranteeing stabilised development - constant growth and little inflation.

However, Mexico is still facing dire poverty and anti-growth policies. Commerce Secretary Raúl Salinas Lozano in particular is a believer that political expediency is holding Mexico back from full development. To him, a remake of the Revolution is needed to focus on hard cash instead of empty platitudes. And foreign deals could be mutually beneficial without giving up Mexican sovereignty.
strings.MEX_CountryInfo_Content_desc.7:
Despite the change in the Revolution and a constitutional ban on reelection, Lázaro Cárdenas is still an extremely popular man, especially for the peasants he has never forgotten. He stands as the most prominent figure fighting against the rightward shift in the party, and has many people behind him and his new manifesto calling for a return to socialism.

Intellectuals and peasant groups have so far been partially satisfied with the Mexican Miracle, but feel more is needed. The growing wealth disparity in the nation, constant corruption, and a dire situation for the countryside have made them increase in popularity. They have already posed a challenge to the system in 1952, backing the leftist opposition. A new voice of the Revolution could rise off of their demands and struggles.
strings.MEX_CountryInfo_Content_desc.8:
Many democracies keep a degree of impartial law enforcement, but the security services of Mexico are another unofficial arm of the PRI. From the corrupt local police to the powerful DFS, the unofficial police state is pervasive throughout the country. These men answer only to the Governor of their states, and the governors only to the President.

Even society itself is not free of the corporatist PRI. Despite nominally free unions, the Confederación de Trabajadores de México takes advantage of its party connections to almost monopolise organized labour. In return, it turns its membership out for the elections, which are counted - yet again - by state apparatuses beholden to the PRI. Likewise the peasants and everyone else have similar organizations that serve to enhance the power of the party, both on the national and the state level.
strings.MEX_CountryInfo_Content_desc.9:
Officially, the PRI rules as a coalition - of groups that are little more than appendages of the state. The only legitimate alternative party to the PRI is the “Partido Acción Nacional”. A party for those excluded by the PRI's corporatist model, its belief in a democratic Mexico is unquestionable. But its meagre existence is only allowed to give the Mexican government some level of legitimacy.

More radical groups exist outside the bounds of legal recognition. The banned Partido Comunista Mexicano and assorted leftist movements exist, and those of a rightist disposition look to the Unión Nacional Sinarquista. However, with them suppressed and the doors to power locked, they face a long and hard road to achieving their goals.
strings.MEX_Plane_Bombing_desc:
The outbreak of war with the Mexicans' puppet has brought the wrath of the Mexican Air Force down upon us. Bombs rain down upon critical infrastructure and military installations and our ability to offer resistance in the air is minimal.

This will disrupt the organisation of our forces and will damage domestic support for the war effort, but we have little choice but to press on and hope that this bombardment does not escalate further.
strings.MEX_military_advisors_desc: Our friends in Mexico have seen fit to dispatch military advisors to aid our armed forces. With their support we shall see a significant improvement in the overall performance of our soldiers, as well as learning important lessons about modern warfare which will improve the efficiency of our armed forces in the future.
strings.MEX_technician_aid_desc: Mexico has seen fit to dispatch technicians to aid our war effort and we are already seeing significant benefits to a range of different areas of our military and economy as a result. We can only hope that aid such as this shall continue to be forthcoming.
strings.MEX_sabotage_effort_desc:
The outbreak of war with the Mexican puppet has resulted in the DFS being unleashed against us. A wave of sabotage and paranoia has swept our country as their agents set to work stealing state secrets, sabotaging military operations, and assassinating officials.

This is proving detrimental to the war effort, not only because of the direct consequences of the sabotage but also because of the paranoia gripping our government as our own agents struggle to prevent further damage.
strings.MEX_PPI_desc: The Dominician Republic is the Latin American harbour for the world's most vile ideology, and has made attempts in the past to support various fascist factions in our home. This cannot stand! Together with our allies in America and Cuba, we shall create a multi-national invasion force so that we may crush Mexico's enemies abroad.
strings.MEX_PP_invasion_text:
The Legion's current £GFX_PHI_supply_texticon Supply is [?USA.US_PP_supply]/100
The Invasion's £GFX_PHI_supply_floor_texticon Minimum Supply is [?USA.US_PP_supply_perc]
strings.MEX_PP_mexican_american_cooperation_ttd: The forces that oppose Trujillo and the fascist regime that rules the Dominican Republic are not from one nation, but several. The relationship between Mexico and the United States will be especially important in working out what will become of the Caribbean's last dictatorship, should it fall.
strings.MEX_PPI_show_infantry_desc: The Caribbean Legionnaire is often green, though they are numerous and willing to give all for the cause.
strings.MEX_PPI_hide_infantry_desc: The Caribbean Legionnaire is often green, though they are numerous and willing to give all for the cause.
strings.MEX_PPI_show_cuban_forces_desc: Cuban battalions are composed of highly-motivated Cuban veterans of their Revolution.
strings.MEX_PPI_hide_cuban_forces_desc: Cuban battalions are composed of highly-motivated Cuban veterans of their Revolution.
strings.MEX_PPI_prepare_cuban_intervention_desc: As our primary ally in the fight against Caribbean Fascism, Cuba has long supported an overthrow of the Trujillo regime. Many revolutionaries and trained soldiers there are chomping at the bit to get at him. Let's not keep them waiting.
strings.MEX_PPI_form_column_tt: If the initial invasion is successful, the Leftists and Nationalists will receive an opinion boost!
strings.MEX_PPI_training_bases_tt: Allows the training of an additional brigade.

strings.MEX_PPI_amphibious_training_desc: Let's face it: there's only one way we are getting to the Dominican Republic. So let's give these landlubbers some sea legs! Our Holguín trainees will take an extended cruise with the Cuban navy practicing hitting the beach.
strings.MEX_PPI_airborne_training_1_tt:
Modify Specialised Training by
Encirclement Penalty: -5.0%
Breakthrough: +5.0%
strings.MEX_PPI_airborne_training_1_desc: Incorporating light STOL aircraft into our force will offer numerous benefits. We will be able to offer a modicum of resupply for forces in remote areas. We can also form small detachments for scouting and special operations.
strings.MEX_PPI_airborne_training_2_tt:
Modify Specialised Training by
Division Experience Gain: +5.0%
Encirclement Penalty: -5.0%
Breakthrough: +5.0%
strings.MEX_PPI_airborne_training_2_desc: With CIA pilots and American equipment, we aren't just discussing supply drops and small unit operations. Now we can talk about resupply, reinforcement, and dropping formations to seize key objectives. And after a few classes at Leeward Point Field, our men can make this a reality.
strings.MEX_PPI_mobilize_resources_desc: Sometimes you need to grease the wheels to make them turn. And a warehouse full of stuff not doing anything is really tempting.
strings.MEX_PPI_organize_supplies_desc: Beans, bullets, bandages - if we do not have enough of these, the invasion goes nowhere. Give the word and we'll procure some more for our boys.
strings.MEX_PPI_provide_guns_desc: If we have some guns laying around somewhere they would do better work in the hands of the Legionnaires. Doesn't matter if they're Thompsons, Garands, or even Porfiriato-era Arisakas; the gun we have is better than the one we don't.
strings.MEX_PPI_rally_oas_support_desc: The Organization of American States may be a tool of Yanqui control over the Americas, but they don't like Trujillo any more than we do. Bringing them into our plan will reap dividends. More than that, it will help assuage the Americans that we want a team effort.
strings.MEX_PPI_unleash_the_dgi_desc: As fearsome as the DFS is, its primary role is within the field of national security with little capacity for foreign intelligence or special operations. The Cuban Dirección General de Inteligencia, on the other hand, is extremely capable in the field of direct action and more than willing to get their hands dirty. We let them loose, and they will set Ciudad Trujillo ablaze.
strings.MEX_PPI_infiltrate_agents_desc: False passports, covert diplomatic postings, parachutes, sneaking ashore, or good old fashioned holes in the fence. The more people we have behind the lines, the more we know, and the more we can do.
strings.MEX_PPI_organize_dissidents_desc: Trujillo, at long last, has finally gone too far. Men and women all across the Republic are ready to take a stand against the monster. We must prepare them for the next chapter of the Latin American revolutionary struggle.
strings.MEX_PPI_work_with_the_cia_desc: Certain American-leaning members of our government have approached us with a proposal. With the FBI working on their own operations to combat Trujillo, would it not make sense to get together on this? There is a lot to be gained by cooperation...
strings.MEX_PPI_mutually_exclusive_with_redirect: Mutually exclusive with Redirect Heat Towards the FBI
strings.MEX_PPI_redirect_heat_towards_the_cia_de: With the FBI working on their own operation against Trujillo, it may be beneficial if we let them take the fall for our benefit. If the SIM is chasing them, it opens up opportunities for us to exploit. It's just business, and what do the Americans know about Latin America anyway?
strings.MEX_PPI_mutually_exclusive_with_working_: Mutually exclusive with Work with the FBI
strings.MEX_PPI_bribe_dominican_officials_desc: Integrity is a rare commodity in a nation full of men who will not stand between Trujillo and their female family members. But we can offer a stipend for those willing to listen to a higher calling. All they have to do is accept what is coming next...
strings.MEX_PPI_the_venezuela_connection_desc: On the other end of the Caribbean is the nation that has long hated Trujillo as much as anyone else - and with good reason! Venezuela has long been itching to get revenge for the SIM assassination of Betancourt, and we can provide. Bringing them into our little scheme will allow us access to their own window into the black spot of the Americas. Plus, they will also be useful in helping Washington and us get on the same page.
strings.MEX_PPI_connect_with_dissidents_desc: Priests, lawyers, hacienda owners, horse trainers, bandits, garbanzo bean farmers - Mexico knows any man can ascend to revolutionary immortality. Those who detest the monster of Santo Domingo just need to see it in others to feel it in themselves. And when the time comes, they will cry out and strike their blow.
strings.MEX_PPI_cruise_the_caribbean_desc: Mexico's navy isn't a big one, but it doesn't mean we can't do more with it. Doing a freedom of navigation exercise near the Dominicans will show them we're ready to reach out and touch them. This will hearten the rebels and Americans, but may spook some of the internal forces at work in the regime.
strings.MEX_PPI_coordinate_with_dgi_desc: As our primary foreign intelligence agency in our bloc, we rely on the Cuban Dirección General de Inteligencia to gather information and conduct operations inside the Dominican Republic. Regular meetings with them will allow for an exchange of information and more coordinated operations together.
strings.MEX_PPI_ceasefire_position_exiles_tt: Increases Juan Bosch's chances at election by 10%.
strings.MEX_PPI_solicit_corporatist_donations_tt: This will increase their Liquid Reserves by $$[?money_reserves_temp|3] B.
strings.MEX_PPI_grant_officers_leave_tt:
Modify Specialised Training by
Division Attack: +5.0%
Division Defense: +5.0%
Breakthrough: +5.0%
strings.MEX_EC_coordinate_with_digepol_desc: The Venezuelan intelligence service, DIGEPOL, is a whir of activity. Though it'll take us both out of the field, a sit-down meeting in Maracaibo will help weave the threads of the plot together.
strings.MEX_EC_disrupt_compromised_communication: Conspiratorial cells are linked by phone and radio - we'll lose valuable intel by intervening, but distant ones will be operating without orders.
strings.MEX_EC_root_out_spies_desc: Moles in DIGEPOL, Iberians in Valencia, all must be arrested and interrogated if Venezuela is to be safe.
strings.MEX_EC_harness_fidels_reach_desc: The Comandante will call Venezuelan peasants, workers, and soldiers to defend their revolution with the vigor and vigilance he has instilled in Havana. The response will be enthusiastic, if untargeted.
strings.MEX_EC_blackmail_potential_dissidents_de: Squeezing the usual Perezjimenistas, even if they're not leading this conspiracy, will turn up what they know about it.
strings.MEX_EC_bribe_venezuelan_officials_desc: Loyalty and patriotism are rare virtures. But greed is a common vice.
strings.MEX_EC_conduct_naval_intelligence_operat: The Caribbean's calm waters disguise dark tides. We'll begin a SEMAR operation to search for foreign interference around Venezuela's coasts.
strings.MEX_EC_trace_caribbean_shipments_desc: Iberian ships sail off Venezuelan waters, lets follow them to their port of call and investigate.
strings.MEX_EC_penetrate_colombian_arms_market_d: If we find who's been buying the Colombians' guns with Iberian pesetas, this plot will be laid wide open.
strings.MEX_EC_infiltrate_border_villages_desc: A traitorous army is massing at the Colombian border near Cúcuta, we need to learn everything about it. How to stop it most of all.
strings.MEX_EC_cooperate_with_the_cru_desc: The Colombian Revolutionary Union is not our first choice of partner - but they owe a great deal to Venezuela's government. We'll work with them to determine the nature of this threat.
strings.MEX_EC_trace_border_activity_desc: Venezuela's western border was difficult to guard before La Violencia, now it's havoc. Let's investigate some of the more major crossings.
strings.MEX_EC_support_pinilla_spies_desc: General Pinilla is a firm ally of Mexico... but his reach into eastern Colombia where we need assistance is limited by the revolutionaries. Let's help his spies infiltrate.
strings.MEX_EC_intercept_arms_and_supplies_desc: Our sources have news of an arms shipment en route from Bogotá. We'll swoop in to grab the supplies and the plotters waiting for them.
strings.MEX_EC_plot_arrests_with_ocae_desc: We've done it. Now let's bag some Venezuelan traitors and Iberian scum.
strings.MEX_aid_ven_commies_tt: We will give communist guerillas weapons to fight against the coupists.
strings.MEX_VC_desc_1:
From the heights of El Hatillo to the banks of the Guaire, they speak of Villalba's old foes, the followers of former dictator Pérez Jiménez, slinking in alleyways. Of officers disenchanted with the military's waning influence. Of a threat to the Venezuelan revolution and the Veracruz Pact.

These whispers are not yet shouts of anger at the walls of Miraflores. Counterrevolutionary forces are still scattered and weak. But the plots of foreign vultures and Villalba's reformist program will give them ample opportunities to metastasize in years to come. We must use the hard lessons taught us by Huerta to scour our ally's streets of infiltrators, reactionaries, and traitors.
strings.MEX_VC_desc_2:
From the heights of El Hatillo to the banks of the Guaire, they speak of Bolivarianist brutes, skulking in barely concealed rage. Of officers disenchanted with the military's waning influence. Of a threat to the Venezuelan revolution and the Veracruz Pact.

These whispers are not yet shouts of anger at the walls of Miraflores. Counterrevolutionary forces are still scattered and weak. But the plots of foreign vultures and Caldera's ambitions as a peacemaker will agitate warmongers in the years to come. We must use the hard lessons taught us by Huerta to scour our ally's streets of infiltrators, reactionaries, and traitors. Or the rats will gnaw their way into Venezuela's foundations.
strings.MEX_CN_deploy_the_best_and_brightest_des: Villalba's URD government boasts impressive technocratic credentials. Let's pull a few members toward the urgent policy challenge of guaranteeing Caracas' security.
strings.MEX_CN_stress_unity_above_all_desc: Caldera's COPEI government is a unifying force. Let's amplify that message on Caracas' streets with tracts and speakers.
strings.MEX_CN_stiffen_miraflores_guard_desc: The president's safety must be ensured from Iberian subversion. The DFS began as Alemán's bodyguards, perhaps they can teach their DIGEPOL equivalents a few tricks.
strings.MEX_CN_monitor_altimira_and_la_praza_fra: Monitor The Plaza Altamira and Golden Mile

The reflecting pool of Altamira Square is a natural gathering point for protestors and intriguers, while the Golden Mile, a financial district with prices among the most expensive in Latin America, may very well paralyze the city if blockaded. Let's establish thorough surveillance over the area.
strings.MEX_CN_establish_commercial_connections_: The businessmen of Baruta always keep their ear to the ground regarding opportunities. A few deals and we'll learn the latest on Iberian smuggling in Caracas.
strings.MEX_CN_stage_student_rallies_desc: Sucre's many universities make the district a natural bastion of opposition to Iberia's reactionary politics. Let's put these radicals to good use for once.
strings.MEX_CN_connect_to_caracas_desc: El Hatillo's height leaves it severed from much of Caracas. We can improve DIGEPOL's access, and soothe residents, by funding new infrastructure.
strings.MEX_CN_send_veracruz_dignitary_desc: The Veracruz Forum brings together the great figures of revolutionary Latin America. A high profile visit to Caracas will energize Venezuela's defenders.
strings.MEX_CN_embed_an_agent_desc: OCAE has improved our coordination with Venezuela's DIGEPOL intelligence service greatly. They'll doubtlessly welcome another DFS tiger roaming the dark alleys of Caracas.
strings.MEX_CN_mobilize_the_ruling_party_desc: Venezuela's government would not be in power without its loyal organizers in Caracas, the beating heart of the country. Let's give a show of strength with a mass rally!
strings.MEX_CN_joint_naval_exercise_in_caracas_b: Joint Naval Exercise in Caracas Bay
Larrazábal's mighty navy helped make the Venezuelan revolution, and now they will defend it. Together with Mexican and Cuban vessels, we will overawe the traitors!
strings.MEX_SalvadoranCoup_NoRevolutionWithoutIn:
-------------
Every time this decision is taken its £political_power_texticon  cost increases by 5.
It increases Castrist Popularity by 30% of Hispanist Popularity if Civilian Anger is 50% or more, and by 15% otherwise.
-------------
Not for nothing do we maintain state control over paper. Let Mexico's intellectual and cultural titans wield their pens, to get Salvadorans to draw their swords.
strings.MEX_SalvadoranCoup_SwordsIntoThorns_desc:
-------------
Every time this decision is taken its £GFX_command_power cost increases by 5.
It decreases Hispanist Popularity by 12% if Civilian Anger is 50% or more, and by 6% otherwise.
-------------
Almazán showed us the dangers of rightist hanger-ons to a Revolution. A DFS-arranged accident for an Hispanist officer now saves the Castrists trouble later.
strings.MEX_SalvadoranCoup_LessonsFromMorelos_de:
-------------
This decision's £GFX_command_power cost increases proportionally to Military Preparedness.
-------------
Corona del Rosal heads the Morelos Group, an officer network covertly spreading PRI influence through our military. Similar techniques can spread Osorio and Rosales' conspiracy through Salvadoran barracks.
strings.MEX_SalvadoranCoup_DoorToDoorRevolutiona:
-------------
The £GFX_weapon_icon  cost of this decision is three times the difference between Military Preparedness and Civilian Anger.
The lower El Salvador's War Support, the more it will increase Military Preparedness.
-------------
Caribbean Legion vets and Castrist soldiers are the most credible voices against the government. Our PRI militancy will teach them a new kind of campaign - the political.
Military Preparedness must exceed Civilian Anger.
strings.MEX_SalvadoranCoup_AJustCause_desc:
-------------
Every time this decision is taken its£GFX_green_dollar_sign cost increases by 5M.
-------------
Alemán can invite a Salvadoran industrialist to Acapulco for business. Explain how profitable it is to be on the right side of a Revolution. They'll get the idea.
strings.MEX_SalvadoranCoup_AJustCause_modifier_t: The Government's Efforts to Combat the Plot will decrease Civilian Anger by 30% less.
strings.MEX_SalvadoranCoup_EmphasizeTheLegacyOfL: Emphasize the Legacy of La Mantanza

-------------
This decision increases the £GFX_flame_texticon of Proletarian Revolts to a maximum of 5. Current power is [?SalvadoranCoup_UnleashProletarianRevolts_Level|Y0].
-------------
Just thirty years ago, Martínez killed tens of thousands to protect the land coffee oligarchs stole. Pamphlets, radios warn Salvadorans to never allow this again.
Popular £GFX_flame_texticon fury has not reached its apex.
Unleash Proletarian Revolts becomes more powerful in creating Civilian Anger.
strings.MEX_SalvadoranCoup_UnleashProletarianRev:
-------------
This decision's power rises as £GFX_flame_texticon does, to a maximum of 5. Current power is [?SalvadoranCoup_UnleashProletarianRevolts_Level|Y0].
-------------
No more shall dispossessed Salvadorans decamp to Honduras in shame. The Castrists will cry out to the masses to fight for their homeland!
strings.MEX_reach_foreign_elites_2_VEN: Reach Out to More Foreign Elites
strings.MEX_FWI_referendum_invite_archimede_desc: Inviting the black Guadeloupe Communist to the Forum will be controversial at home and abroad, but will raise her profile in the struggle for independence. Her speech will be in French anyway, so the risk of communist contagion is low.
strings.MEX_FWI_referendum_fund_pcg_protests_des: The Guadeloupe Communist Party is among the most effective advocates against the U.S. Confederation Plan. Backed by pesos, they can turn out opponents in Les Abymes.
strings.MEX_FWI_referendum_publish_discourse_on_: Poet and politician Aimé Césaire has condemned U.S. colonialism with the same vehemence as he did the French. A book deal with the Fondo de Cultura Económica would fund his advocacy against the Confederation.
strings.MEX_FWI_referendum_agitate_in_fort_de_fr: The shantytowns of Martinique hold those most harmed by the Civil Administration's failures. We only need to remind them of this, and get them to the polls.
strings.MEX_FWI_referendum_soothe_tempers_desc: A few pulled punches in the Caribbean and conversations with Fulton and Scott in the Federal District will remind the gringos that our 'involvement' in the Antilles is nothing but a show for domestic consumption.
strings.MEX_FWI_referendum_critique_operation_up: The North Americans' botched development planning has mired Guadeloupe and Martinique in poverty. Get a scathing report to businessmen and bureaucrats on the islands, and they'll see the need to chart their own course.
strings.MEX_FWI_referendum_decry_the_occupation_: President Madrazo himself will speak on the injustice of ongoing U.S. interference in Antilles affairs. The speech may be in Spanish, but the righteous thunder is universal.
strings.MEX_FWI_referendum_send_ctm_envoys_desc: The New Deal policies the U.S. foisted on the Antilles have led to strong unions on the islands. Perhaps our own workers can tempt them away by showing them the fruits of Mexican labor.
strings.MEX_FWI_referendum_send_ctm_envoys_tt: Workers enjoying high power in the PRI will increase the effectiveness of this decision.
strings.MEX_FWI_referendum_rush_in_francophone_d: We lack any substantial diplomatic facilities in the Guadeloupe and Martinique. If we want to properly manage this opportunity, we need French-speakers like Pepe Gallástegui there yesterday.
strings.MEX_FWI_referendum_train_in_election_tec: Certain Antilles community leaders are known opponents of U.S. dominance. With a little instruction in voting carousels and pre-filled ballot boxes, they'll be even more effective ones.
strings.MEX_FWI_referendum_highlight_us_interfer: Of course the gringos will prevent the realization of national self-determination - they've done it in the Antilles for two decades now! But to truly rile up their foes, we'll need a few concrete examples...
This decision will become more powerful if the confederationists hold a polling advantage.
strings.MEX_FWI_referendum_involve_our_dominican: Involve Our Allies in the Dominican Republic
Our Dominican allies will lend their voices to the referendum campaign, tilting another Caribbean domino in our direction.
strings.MEX_PP_ceasefire_balaguer_tt: The Mexican government will be very upset with this...
strings.MEX_Puerto_Plata.1.desc:
DIRECCIÓN FEDERAL DE SEGURIDAD

ISSUE: SIM assassination attempt within the Federal District.

At approximately 22:15 this evening, two agents of the Dominican Military Intelligence Service, or SIM, attempted to assassinate Juan Bosch as he returned to his hotel in the Federal District's Zona Rosa.

The DFS had been informed of a likely effort by a source within the Trujillo administration, and established protective surveillance around Bosch, the primary leader of the Dominican opposition, upon his arrival in Mexico. Noting a Toyota with shaded windows trailing Bosch's taxi for multiple blocks, a DFS agent rammed the vehicle with his own while calling for backup. Two armed men fled the Toyota, but were pursued and dispatched by multiple agents in a firefight.

The profile of one of the assassins matched a known SIM agent, but the other was unknown to DFS sources. Both possessed high-quality fabricated documents identifying them as Banco de Comercio employees and carrying modern German armaments. Agents are currently attempting to identify SIM contacts, safehouses, or entry points used by the two men, but progress has been slowed by injuries sustained in the operation.

Until such time as those assets are seized and the lack of additional infiltrators confirmed, Bosch's safety cannot be guaranteed. The Trujillo government has also responded to past defeats by targeting Mexican security and political officials. Further espionage operations by the Dominican Republic constitute an escalating threat to national security.

Respectfully,

Captain Luis de la Barreda Moreno
strings.MEX_Puerto_Plata.1.a: Forward immediately to President López Mateos.
strings.MEX_Puerto_Plata.2.desc:
Fernando Gutiérrez Barrios, DFS captain, met many would-be revolutionaries in his line of work. They answered his questions, and then would not be heard from again. How special then, to receive a message, not from yet another communist or synarchist agitator, but from a true revolutionary. From Fidel Castro.

The two had become acquainted in inauspicious circumstances. In '56, Gutiérrez had trailed the Cuban and his guerillas as they plotted Batista's downfall from a ranch in Mexico State. The first time Castro saw his face, Fernando was slapping handcuffs on him.

But in the interrogations that followed, Castro's words had not been those of a criminal but those of a revolutionary out to topple a Cuban Huerta. Or those of a possible asset for Mexico. They came to... an arrangement, and Gutiérrez Barrios arranged for the dissidents' release. As the rebels set sail from Túxpam to their homeland, the duo had shaken hands.

The telegram now in that same hand carried congratulations on Gutiérrez's promotion and anodyne tales of Castro's latest hunting and fishing. Their typical friendly correspondence... until the Dominican Question arose.

Castro argued that the time was right to rid Hispaniola of its tinpot fascist dictator. The Republic's German patrons are spread thin, and old allies like the Church are growing estranged. Abbes and his SIM are briefly shaken by the failed assassination attempt on Bosch. The June 14th urban guerillas are swelling in strength, fueled by dissatisfaction among the Dominican youth and middle class. Three years of Mexican and Cuban subversion efforts are now coalescing into a perfect storm.

Gutiérrez Barrios would alert Secretary Díaz Ordaz and the President of this temporary opportunity, along with his recommendation to take full advantage of it.
strings.MEX_Puerto_Plata.2.a: He and Castro had brought down one Caribbean dictator. There was one to go.
strings.MEX_Puerto_Plata.3.desc:
“Always a pleasure to speak with you Adolfo,” began Castro, “and thank you for accommodating my busy schedule.”

López Mateos knew of the Cuban leader's nocturnal habits, but a midnight meeting was certainly a stretch. The mug of black coffee was held as tightly in his left hand as the telephone receiver was in his right. Pulling the latter closer to his mouth, “Certainly Fidel, Captain Gutiérrez informs me that you're considering action against the Trujillo regime. What is your plan, and what are you asking of us?”

“A coup. We both want Trujillo and Batista in coffins and the rest of the regime swept away. It's splintering, Adolfo, civilian leaders and generals are already covertly reaching out to our assets and yours. We push and the rest of the rats jump overboard.”

El Comandante continued, “My request is to establish an office for joint intelligence operations in Havana. Tomorrow morning, Captain Gutiérrez will send you the brief on the Oficina Conjunta de Asuntos Externos, or OCAE, as we've been calling it. The strength of our Dominican networks would grow fivefold if we united them. This Joint Office of Foreign Affairs would gather together dissidents and exiles like the June 14th Movement and help organize the Caribbean Legion.”

López Mateos had been sneaking a surreptitious swig of coffee, just as Gutiérrez had apparently been sneaking around with Castro and going around the chain of command. Their choice of allies was worrisome too. Here in Mexico, the Caribbean Legion were kept under tight watch, but who knows what those squabbling crypto-communists would get up to in Hispaniola. But... if anyone could overthrow a monstrous Caribbean dictator, it was these two. And Gutiérrez could be counted on to keep the radicals in check. “You have Mexico's support, Fidel. I'll approve this OCAE, and Captain Gutiérrez will have the leeway and funds he needs.”
strings.MEX_Puerto_Plata.3.a: We're avenging '48 no matter the cost.
strings.MEX_Puerto_Plata.3_tt: £GFX_decision_icon_small Decisions to oust Trujillo will be unlocked.
strings.MEX_Puerto_Plata.4.desc:
Two of the Federal District's leading spies sat a table-length apart. Washington's man, Winston Scott, was voluble, speaking in Spanish at length about the US's planned naval and aviation support for the Puerto Plata landing. From memory, he laid out the targets of the saboteurs that would spring into action once the Caribbean Legion got to shore. The capstone was a plot to coup Trujillo and usher in a joint civil-military government.

Winston claimed that high-ranking military officials were prepared to move as soon as El Jefe was dead. And it wouldn't be of old age. The FBI had already smuggled M14 rifles and thousands of dollars to a group of insiders, including a member of Trujillo's personal guard.

At that last point, Mexico's Fernando Gutiérrez Barrios broke his silence, “Amado García Guerrero. The DFS is likewise supplying that group through General Díaz, though we've prioritized connecting them with sympathetic regime members rather than providing material.” To Winston's cocked eyebrow, he responded, “A different Díaz, Modesto, and another well-placed man who saved Juan Bosch's life.”

“Interesting...” Winston replied, drumming his fingers on the table, “And how could the FBI be of assistance to the DFS?”

“We're working to coordinate the various June 14th cells into a broader uprising. If your saboteurs prioritize disrupting SIM communications around Santiago the day of the invasion, I anticipate the successful seizure of the city center. The Legion will then have a clear path of advance toward Ciudad Trujillo.”
strings.MEX_Puerto_Plata.5.desc:
“God of power and mercy, maker of love and peace...” Born in 1943 in Mexico City, young Andre Santana had to contend with a world built on the backs of exploitation and intentional ignorance. His father was constantly burned out from his job assembling car doors in the Ford plant. His mother worked part time as a maid to an expat family from Kumamoto. His older brother hawked wood carvings on the street. But his Grandfather... his Grandfather was a proud peasant who had refused to take the abuse from the Haciendas, and joined the División del Norte. To hear him tell of his time on his horse with a 30-30 Carbine, Andre's Grandfather was one of the last of a generation of men, before modern capitalism had broken their backs.

“To know you is to live, and to serve you is to reign...” The white sands of Puerto Plata stretched as far as Andre could see, dividing the Dominican city from the endless blue sky and sea. By his side were men of every type and persuasion - Mexican boys like him, veterans of the Cuban Revolution, Dominican dissidents, revenge-seeking Hatians, and Yanquis just willing to fight. This was more than the vaqueros and American cowboys Grandfather stood with. The whole of the Americas was coming together to destroy tyranny, injustice, ignorance -

“Through the intercession of Michael the Archangel, be our protection against all evil...” But Andre's stomach was in knots. He was not in Mexico City. He was in a foreign land, a hostile land, full of Fascists and Hitlerites who wanted him dead. If he made a mistake, he would die. He was marching toward the Faro, the iconic lighthouse of the city. Perhaps his training was the only thing that kept him moving and not collapsing from fright.

“Help me overcome war and violence and establish your law of love and justice...” The black SIM Volkswagens were coming down the road. Andre's commander yelled for them to take cover. As Andre sighted the lead car with his AR-10, he finished his prayer, hopefully not his last.
strings.MEX_Puerto_Plata.5.a: Grant this through Christ our Lord. Amen.

strings.MEX_Puerto_Plata.6.desc:
To Secretary Ordaz, Captain Gutiérrez Barrios:

I am sincerely glad that Trujillo has been eliminated in line with our preparations. However, in light of the failure of the plan's second stage, a prompt update as to the capabilities of the incumbent regime - and its inner workings - must be delivered to my office at your earliest convenience.

Dear Secretary Olachea:

Any munitions that can still be recovered from our arms dumps must be sent back to Veracruz immediately. You are more than capable of handling this.

Secretary of External Relations Barraud:

Arrange a telephone call with Castro as soon as possible. Plotting a big help, yes, but only to a certain extent (Pupo did not materialize). Legion will be backed insofar as we can provide maximum aid without violating the Estrada Doctrine.

López Mateos looked over the pieces of paper strung out across his desk. Was there someone he had forgotten? His calloused grew turgid as the fountain pen grew heavier. Ah, yes -

Greetings Licenciado Cárdenas:

Despite our disagreements, I believe you can look to our progress fighting the fascist Trujillo regime in Hispaniola to see that we are both fighting for the same revolution -

He crossed out the last few words with a thick line. Fighting on common ground? Fighting for common beliefs? No - enough semantics. Perhaps some things were better left unsaid.
strings.MEX_Puerto_Plata.6.a: López Mateos felt the letter crumple in his hands as he slowly ripped it in two.
strings.MEX_Puerto_Plata.7.desc:
Luis gazed out of the bubble canopy into the Caribbean night. With their beacon lights off, he could only spot the other aircraft by the stars they obscured. 25 holes in the night sky, bound for an airfield in southern Cuba that didn't exist on any map. The only noise in the cockpit was the dull roar of the jet engine. They had been ordered to keep their radios off for the duration of the flight. The higher-ups didn't want the Dominicans to know the squadron was being moved to Cuba. It wasn't without risk; it could be difficult to keep track of other airplanes at the best of times. To say it was harder when you couldn't speak with your squadmates was an understatement.

Complications arose when the planes soared into a towering cloud bank that stretched away to the horizon in both directions. What little frame of reference Luis had suddenly disappeared. The only thing keeping him airborne and on the flight path were the glowing dials on the instrument panel. Suddenly, a bout of turbulence struck Luis's plane. He managed to keep control over the aircraft, and nudged the stick forward to descend out of the lashing air currents. Glancing down at the instrument panel, he noted that he had nearly 100 meters of altitude. He was just thankful he didn't slam into one of the other planes.

The cloud must have been several kilometers wide. It took the better part of an hour to pass through. When Luis emerged, there was no sign of his comrades. Only the brilliant array of stars above, and the lights of a ship lazily drifting in the warm ocean below. Luckily, he had not strayed far enough off course to miss the Cuban coastline. Navigation over land was much easier. After lining up the lights of the towns with the maps provided for him, it was just a matter of pointing the plane in the right direction.

Another hour passed in silence before he spotted the airfield. A cluster of intersecting dirt runways illuminated by dim bulbs well over a mile from the closest village. He circled once, saw the runway was clear, and brought his plane down. After he taxied his plane to the side, a battered jeep rolled up to his plane to ferry him to the barracks for some much needed sleep. Climbing into the passenger seat, he asked the driver if anyone else had arrived yet.
strings.MEX_Puerto_Plata.7_tt: The leased aircraft will return to us, even if the Legion fails...
strings.MEX_Puerto_Plata.8.desc:
The President, in his agitation, did not pay heed to the lack of moonlight shining into the National Palace from the skylight, with a flickering lamp the only bulb to stave off the darkness.

On any other ordinary day, he would be able to have it fixed. But this was no ordinary day.

The Caribbean Legion lines had collapsed into full rout. The June 14th dissidents in the capital fared no better, with the tightened repression of the new regime and breakthroughs at the front sparking a mass flight to the Haitian border. Others, desperate for a sea evacuation, overwhelmed docks and harbours across Puerto Plata to seek their escape, pleading to the innocent, inconspicuous trawlers across the way - Mexican trawlers, that is - that have been covertly supplying the Legion ever since its campaign began in earnest.

López Mateos, in his thoughts, realised the nation had not come as close to diplomatic catastrophe since the Nazis forced Camacho's hand after they attacked Mexican oil tankers - to say nothing of the Guatemalans opening fire on his countrymen's fishing boats back in 1959.

He would be endangering the lives of all of these sailors if he gave the order to move in. The Dominican Armed Forces could very well glass them to pieces in the sea...

But he had started this. He had to finish it.

Picking up the telephone, López Mateos made a priority call.
strings.MEX_Puerto_Plata.8.a: “As many as you can on the boats, then get the hell out of there!”
strings.MEX_Puerto_Plata.9.desc:
López Mateos sat hunched over his desk, one hand clutching the presidential receiver in a vice grip and the other ushering DFS Captain,, Fernando Gutiérrez Barrios, to come over. Dial tone. “Operator. You know who it is.”

Castro's groggy voice filtered through the other end after a click. “...what is the meaning of this, Excellency?” It was pitch black outside in the small hours, something that only became apparent to the President when he swivelled in his office chair; it would be at least dusk in Havana by now. Gutiérrez Barrios, by now sitting adjacent to López Mateos, sat rigid, ears attentive and hanging off every word.

“We can no longer count on Nixon's support, Fidel. He's fucked us. He's with that fascist stooge,” López Mateos practically spat out the name. “Balaguer.”Castro erupted into inaudible shouting at the other end. López Mateos took a breath, stood; still wrestling with the telephone cord. “The last time we suffered a betrayal of such calibre was when they snuffed out democracy and murdered Madero so they could put that bastard Huerta in, all the way back in 1913! And then over the Aleutians, Nixon went behind my back and deceived Secretary Ordaz! These are no aberrations, Fidel, these were deliberate crimes - all to further their own interests.”

“We need a plan of action, Excellency. What will Mexico do?”

López Mateos let out a laugh, quickly sizzled out in the heat of his rage as he gestured and pointed with fervour. “We continue as planned. The Legion will get our full support, weapons, intelligence, munitions. As for the gringos?” He tightened his fists. “Your people, my people, the DGI - we are going to find every last one of them still in Hispaniola and we are going to drive them into the fucking sea.”
strings.MEX_Puerto_Plata.10.desc:
“I must say that I felt the heartbeat of Revolution today, Adolfo,” Fidel Castro relaxed in the plush lounging chair in the quarter of Los Pinos reserved for the highest-ranked foreign dignitaries. After a stuffy but jovial official dinner, Presidents Castro and Mateos were joined by DFS captain and personal friend Gutiérrez Barrios in a more private meeting for dessert. However, Castro had no sweets to offer but fine tobacco and coffee. Instead, some Dominican cake was ferried in from a nearby celebration for the Caribbean Legion.

“I feel it too. The hearts of our three nations beat in harmony now,” Mateos sipped gently at the coffee, letting its bitterness mix with the lingering sweetness of the cake's Italian meringue icing. “The regime's defeat is a great opportunity to expand our influence in the Caribbean. I hope that this revolutionary spirit can spread.”

“It was electric out there. Your people sure know how to show their appreciation.” Castro thought back on the only just recently passed parade he headed. He and the Cuban contingent of the Caribbean Legion had come to Mexico City to celebrate the liberation of the Dominican Republic. “The people will see sweet opportunity fall into their laps. It is all thanks to our great work, Adolfo. And, of course, I must thank you for your contributions, Captain.”

Gutiérrez politely nodded at the Cuban president before speaking up. “I'm glad you are so optimistic, but we are not completely finished with the island. My sources indicate that Legion radicals appear to be organizing a Marxist coup.”

“They can try all they like. The heartbeat of revolution beats with us.” A wry smile pierced through the Cuban's teeth and the titular cigar that sat between them. “Now tonight Gutiérrez. Loosen up, enjoy the celebrations, and have some dessert. Your job as spymaster will still be there in the morning.”
strings.MEX_Puerto_Plata.10.a: It is best not to sugarcoat the realities of victory.
strings.MEX_Puerto_Plata.11.desc:
For a moment, sweet. Then President López Mateos got kicked in the mouth.

Before the taste of his second shot of tequila subsided, he started pouring the third since news of the Caribbean Legion's calamitous failure reached Los Pinos. It would have been his fifth had he not spent twenty minutes berating Ordaz before dispatching him to shut down the Legion training camps and cover up any trace of Mexican involvement. Trujillo's assassins would be coming for him soon enough, he didn't want to be hiding from foreign journalists as well.

A knock on the door. Salinas' voice on the other side, “Forgive me, Your Excellency, but I'd like to share something that may be useful in this difficult time.” A brusque grunt was sufficient welcome for the Secretary, who entered bearing a bottle of fine sake. The president and the norteño locked eyes... and laughed.

Soon the duo were barely upright, a small forest of shot glasses surrounding them on the president's desk. For perhaps the third time, Salinas shared his theory of what had gone wrong, “You shee, Adolfo, it's typical Yanqui adventurism. Washington wants to dominate their shurroundings, they couldn't risk a shtrong or independent Legion. They ensnare us in their half-baked plan and then pull the punch.”

A small voice in López Mateos mind called out that he and Castro had decided to back Trujillo's overthrow all on their own. Had cast away the lives of countless young men willing to fight for freedom. Had stretched and bent the Estrada Doctrine for the sake of a fool's errand.

A swig straight from the bottle drowned that voice. His own croaked out, “Damn right, Raúl. Damn right.”
strings.MEX_Puerto_Plata.12.desc:
Gustavo Díaz Ordaz prided himself on keeping a straight face against all challenges. Fernando Gutiérrez Barrios had learned to play his cards straight to his chest, to conceal his true feelings. But a brief glance between the two was mutually understood - neither knew why they were here. All they knew was that López Mateos had called them to his office in the Palacio Nacional at once.

After a few moments of unacknowledgement, López Mateos reached under a stack of papers and pulled out a book. A textbook - for secondary schoolers. On the cover were drawings of Zapata, Villa, and Obregón. “This,” López Mateos began, “is the first standardized textbook on the Mexican Revolution. Because of our efforts, every child in Mexico will receive it free of charge in their history class. They can hear the same stories, see the same heroes, and understand the truth of the Revolution. And they can understand our need to fight ignorance and poverty today as these men fought against Díaz and Huerta back then. But there's a problem with it.” Ordaz and Barrios stared blankly.

“We just wrote another book about the revolution - but we can't publish it.” A smile broke across his face. “We crushed another dictatorship, not at home, but abroad. We stood up and put a stop to Trujillo. We showed the world the Mexican Revolution isn't Mexican; every man in Latin America can follow the trail we tread and end the universal evils of disenfranchisement and neglect. Make no mistake; this is one of the proudest moments in the history of Mexico - but if even a fraction of the story got out, we would be crucified for it.

”I cannot shout it from that balcony over there like the Grito, we cannot celebrate it like the Oil Expropriation, we cannot put this new book into the hands of every Mexican child. But I can tell you exactly how I feel right now, if I cannot tell the world or Mexico itself. And eventually our nation will know what we have accomplished in the Dominican Republic.“
strings.MEX_Puerto_Plata.12.a: “Now, do we want rum or tequila?”
strings.MEX_Puerto_Plata.13.desc:
“It was a powerful speech, but only if words could kill,” Fidel Castro said, gripping a glass of whisky on the rocks dangerously tight. López Mateos paced a high balcony overlooking Havana, even the pastel buildings lining the city's wide streets could not distract him from his indignation.

“When you're as powerful as us, they ought to.” Mateos scrunched the piece of paper that held his personal speech notes and addendums, his writers never fully grasped his passion. He had flown to the Cuban capitol to try and salvage some shred of international dignity after being juked twice, first by Nixon switching sides to Balaguer and then by the Legion itself signing on to this farce of a Santo Domingo Agreement. He was forced to get up on a stage with Castro and publicly lambast the people he was just supporting. He and Castro spent the morning delivering a joint statement declaring the Agreement a betrayal of the Dominican Republic's aspirations for liberty and independence as envisioned by Duarte. “Where did it all go so wrong? Everything was in place.”

“The bastards don't know what's good for them.” Under the colorful awning, Castro shaded his shared anger with cool words. “They should know better than to get in bed with the Yanquis, or to dirty their hands embracing fascists.”

“I never should have trusted that wicked crook Nixon after the Aleutian affair.” Mateos stepped into the shade and grabbed a waiting glass of cool water. The condensation wet his hands as he gulped passionately at the refreshing liquid. “Nor the pack of mercenaries and scoundrels that call themselves the Caribbean Legion.”

“Ignore those who failed you.” Castro grimaced at the implications of Mateos' wide-reaching condemnation. Instead of a retort, Castro offered his hand to the haranguing president. “You have my word. Mexico and Cuba will always stand together.”
strings.MEX_Puerto_Plata.13.a: “Yes, Good friends are hard to find.”
strings.MEX_Puerto_Plata.14.desc:
The Dominican city of Puerto Plata was electric with celebratory zeal from the common man to the highest politicians. On one of the many beautiful beaches that dot the city's coast López Mateos stands with General Pupo Román and Fidel Castro as they watch the ships of Legionnaires returning to Cuba depart from the harbor. Like one of the American cowboy movies, the victorious Legion rides into the sunset. Deep reds and yellows splashed across the blue ocean like fireworks cascading across the sky. All along the coast Dominicans cheer in joyous celebration. They drink in the streets. Some ascend onto the former trujillista jail that overlooks the sea, the Fortaleza San Felipe. Many take to the beach itself.

Mateos looks at the sand, sea, and people jealously. Deep down, he wished he could rip off his suit and join them. To splash and play in a way befitting the joy of the day. Instead, he let their display fill his heart. He never thought he'd stand in the Dominican Republic, let alone one freed from Trujillo's tyranny. Mateos turns to Román with a tear in his eye. “Thank you, General, for inviting me to join you for this historic moment. I will hold onto this memory dearly.”

“You are too kind. You deserve to be here.” Román gripped the Mexican President's arm in a handshake. “Thank you. The Republic would not be liberated; I would not walk freely on this beach without Mexico's aid.” Mateos pulled Román's handshake into a hug. They embraced as warmly as two male politicians could. In the distance, news cameras flashed to capture the friendship of nations and the freedom to be happy.

“Now, Your Excellency,” Román continued. “I believe an exquisite dinner has been prepared for us.”

“That sounds nice.” Mateos looked back out to the kaleidoscopic horizon, “But give me ten minutes. I wish to watch the sunset.”
strings.MEX_Puerto_Plata.14.a: Soon a new day will dawn for the Dominican Republic.

strings.MEX_econ_stimulation_detailed:
The economic stimulation of {getmexeconregionthecontext3}{root_getmexeconregionnamecontext3} is [?MEX_econ_region_selected:MEX_econ_region_stimulation_percent|Y2%%].
 This increases our regional GDP Growth by [?temp_stim_gdpg|G3%%], due to a base impact of [?temp_gdp_growth_base|G3%%] and a multiplier of [?temp_urb_multiplier|G2%%] from our urban population.

Every two weeks, economic stimulation decreases by [?temp_stim_decay|R2%%] towards a floor of [?MEX_econ_region_selected:MEX_econ_region_base_stimulation_percent|Y2%%].
 This comes from a base stimulation decay of [?MEX_econ_region_selected:MEX_econ_region_stimulation_decay|2R%%]
 mitigated by [?MEX_econ_region_selected:MEX_econ_region_quality_of_life_stimulation_decay_modifier|2Y%%] by Urban Quality of Life.

This region is saddled with {mex_econ_map_debt} of debt.
 Exceeding the local limit of {mex_econ_map_debt_limit} will have dire consequences at the end of each year.
 In the meantime, debt further decreases local economic activity by [?temp_debt_stim_impact|R2%%] monthly.

The regional debt limit is annually calculated as the sum of [?MEX.MEX_econ_GDP_debt_limit_conversion|0Y%] of regional GDP and [?MEX.MEX_econ_debt_debt_limit_conversion|0Y%] of local debt.
 This value ebbs and flows with the needs and capabilities of the region, but if it were to be immediately reset, the new limit would be $${mex_econ_graph_debt_limit_projection}.

Forecasts predict this region's economy will grow by [?temp_gdpg|G3%%] this year.
 We estimate that the region's coffers will net a quarter (1/4) of regional growth.

 The value of the region's exports return to Mexico twofold, as $$[?temp_cash_crop_revenue|3]B of national revenue and
 [?temp_cash_crop_pus|Y2] £tt_prod_unit Production Units.
 Commercial agriculture accelerates migration to urban centers by [?temp_cash_crop_migration|2%%].

[?MEX_econ_region_selected:MEX_econ_region_agronomics_staple_crop_percent|Y2%%] of regional farming is dedicated to staple crops - maize, beans, and more - for consumption.
 The local provision of foodstuffs improves the quality of life in the entire region by [?temp_staple_qol|2%%].

This region's farms are [?MEX_econ_region_selected:MEX_econ_region_agronomics_productivity_percent|Y2%%] productive.
 Local productivity contributes [?temp_prod_pus|Y2] £tt_prod_unit Production Units to the nation.
 However, the mechanization of agriculture also accelerates urban migration by [?temp_prod_migration|2Y%%].
 Additionally, it decreases regional debts by $$[?temp_prod_debt_dec|2]M monthly.

Altogether, Mexico nets a total of [?temp_net_agr_pus|Y0] £tt_prod_unit Production Units gained from agriculture nationally.
